thread:
maria: Thinking about adding a candidate-TTL header to rerank requests so we can route short-lived candidates to fast/cheap models and drop stale candidates earlier. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

jason: I like the idea. Main tradeoff: billing/quota math and KV-cache correctness. If we drop candidates client-side vs server-side we need consistent accounting for score-units.

alex: Console UX ask: can we expose a per-route toggle + sample rate for TTL routing? e.g., show expected cost delta and estimated p99 latency impact.

maria: Yes. UX should default off, with a visualization showing rejected-candidate ratio if enabled. Also need sensible default TTL (like 300ms) rather than forcing app teams to guess.

ben: If TTL is a routing hint, not a hard contract, we need a clear wire field. Proposal: add header `X-Candidate-TTL-ms` and optional `X-Rerank-PriorityTag` so routing can prefer variants.

sara: Backwards compat: if header absent treat as infinite TTL (current behavior). And we must ensure model selection fallback when fast models can't cover fanout. No silent drops.

jason: Implementation constraints: batching window math already assumes token/lifetime distributions. We'll add a small pre-routing step to classify candidates into TTL-buckets then pick model variant. Need to ensure KV-cache lookup keys include TTL bucket if cache coherence matters.

maria: Example request snippet we discussed:

```
POST /v1/rerank
Headers:
  Authorization: Bearer ...
  X-Candidate-TTL-ms: 250
  X-Rerank-PriorityTag: low-latency
Body: { candidates: [...], query: "..." }
```

alex: For telemetry we should emit: `rerank.ttl_bucket`, `rerank.ttl_dropped`, `rerank.fallback_variant`, and sample `rerank.sampled_candidates` payloads behind a feature flag for privacy.

ben: Quota effects: TTL routing will map to different model variants which have different score-unit costs. We need to expose per-variant unit accounting in the console and aggregate per-route cost projection when TTL toggles are enabled.

sara: Canary plan: roll to 10% of traffic with `canary-ttl-2026` tag. Monitor p99 latency, ttl_drop ratio, and regression in top-k ordering (we'll run evals on preserved prompt sets).

jason: Agree. Also add a conservative backoff: if variant capacity < threshold, route to default model (no TTL enforcement) instead of dropping. Dropping should only happen as last resort and be visible in trace IDs.

maria: For dashboard, add a small panel: TTL heatmap vs throughput + an explainer flyout. UX: allow toggling preview cost/latency before enabling for prod. :rocket:

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary `canary-ttl-2026` rolled out to rerank-runtime v1.14 on eng-staging at 2026-03-20T14:18:00Z

ben: One more nit: scoring envelope needs a small field `meta.ttl_bucket` returned so clients can understand why candidate was scored/routed. That helps debugging.

sara: Agree but keep response size tiny. `meta.ttl_bucket` can be an enum string.

maria: Okay next steps: jason/eng to prototype routing classifier + variant mapping, ben to update billing shim and console projection, alex/product to design toggle and heatmap, sara to draft canary playbook and eval hooks. I'll track in the rerank TTL RFC doc. Thanks everyone! :thumbsup:
